Posted February 6, 2001
The Changing Environment for Marijuana Reform -- Analysis By Richard Cowan

MarijuanaNews.com generally confines itself to the issues regarding cannabis in its various forms, but I think that it is useful from time to time to review not just the state of the marijuana reform movement, but also the environment in which it is operating.

First, the good news.

Although the 1970s saw many changes in the marijuana laws, today marijuana prohibition is under assault as never before. There are a number of reasons for this.

Obviously, the medical marijuana movement has been helpful in raising the issue, as has the drive to allow DEAland farmers to be able to grow industrial hemp, like their counterparts in most of the rest of the industrialized world, including China and Russia.

However, in some ways, the opposition to the medical marijuana and hemp have been as important to the general anti-prohibitionist movement as those supporting them. This may seem odd, but the fact is that the prohibitionists never look worse than when they are trying to justify arresting the sick and dying – or when they are claiming that the farmers are a part of a plot to legalize all drugs for children.

The fact is that the various medical marijuana laws have passed over the almost unanimous opposition of the states’ establishments. Oddly, this was even the case in Hawaii, where the legislature passed and the governor signed their medical marijuana law. The state medical association lied to try to kill the law, as have medical associations in other states.
See
Organized Quacks In Hawaii Continue To Support Arresting The Sick and Dying

Criticism of marijuana prohibition by the governors of New Mexico and Minnesota have also been very helpful in raising the issue. New Mexico’s Gary Johnson is even going to be the keynote speaker at the NORML conference in April. We have come a long way.

Outside of DEAland the situation is even better. Canada is committed to having a medical marijuana program by the middle of the year and will probably " decriminalize " marijuana as well.
See
Canadian Health Minister Supports " Decriminalization " and Medical Marijuana. Apparently…

Belgium has decriminalized possession and cultivation. The Swiss say they are going to legalize soon. Elsewhere the world is moving in our direction.
See
Belgium To Decriminalize Possession and Cultivation for Personal Use. No Coffeeshops, Yet.
and
Swiss Commission Denounces Marijuana Prosecutions As " An Arbitrary Act of Coercion ".
and
We Are Winning: Jamaica To Establish National Commission On Ganja; Dutch, Germans and Swiss to Hold Conference in the Spring.

When the good news is also the bad news…

The marijuana reform movement is also being helped along by the growing recognition that the " Drug War " is a " failure. " However, regular readers know that I object to calling marijuana prohibition a " failure " – although it has certainly failed to achieve its supposed goals.

When I say that marijuana prohibition is not just a failure, but really a counterproductive fraud, I am not trying to score rhetorical points. Marijuana prohibition is actually making all of the substance abuse problems worse and is based on almost a century of deliberate government lying. It is not some " noble experiment " that worked out badly.
See
New Mexico Drug Advisory Group Recommends Decriminalization Of Marijuana For Personal Use. Urges End to Government Lying.
and
Bizarro to Leave after the First of the Year! Goes Out Lying.
and
Drug Czar Uses Foreign Affairs Magazine Article For Anti-Dutch Propaganda,
Elevating The Lying To Official Status. Analysis By Richard Cowan

I think that policy makers need to understand that marijuana prohibition is not something that they can ignore, while they deal with the " more serious " problems of hard drug use.
See
Marijuana Legalization, The Missing Pillar in Solving the Substance Abuse Problem in Vancouver and All of Canada. Analysis By Richard Cowan

Unfortunately, that is the tendency of many in the political end of the harm reduction movement. I have complained from time to time about the efforts to subsume the marijuana reform movement into the broader drug legalization and/or harm reduction movements.
See
Legalize? " Marijuana Maybe " Says Soros Spokesman

The hit movie, Traffic, may also be feeding this view of the war as a " failure, " but " new " drugs in DEAland are also creating new issues.

Ecstasy and meth and now Oxy.

Three new developments that both help and hurt the marijuana reform movement is the emergence of the Ecstasy and Oxy markets and the resurgence of methamphetamine. Although E and meth are chemically somewhat similar, their markets could not be more different.

To put it bluntly, the E market is upscale and arresting its users and small scale sellers poses political risks for the prohibitionists. It even has its own advocacy group, Dancesafe.

(The prohibitionists do like to blame the smuggling of Ecstasy on the Dutch, but the emergence of the Israelis as major suppliers, creates other problems for them. Happily, anti-Semitism is politically incorrect, unlike lying about the Dutch or marijuana.)

On the other hand, meth and Oxycontin, a new synthetic opiate, have downscale markets, particularly poor whites, and this group is almost as expendable as inner-city black crack users. They could be the cannon fodder for a whole new front in the Drug War, especially when the war in Colombia becomes a bit too much of a bother. Unfortunately for the prohibitionists, there is growing resistance to the enormous cost of prisons and the related industries.

I am not going to say anything about the risks in using these drugs, because the history of marijuana prohibition shows that that risk is irrelevant to the laws passed and the methods of enforcement.

However, it is clear that meth has become the new scourge du jour for the prohibitionists and the media. Will the prohibitionists really be able to continue their war on marijuana, when meth makes such an attractive target? Similarly, will middle class parents worry as much about marijuana, when their kids may be using E, or worse, a counterfeit E?

The biggest problem that we face is still the very annoying fact that marijuana reform movement is the Rodney Dangerfield of issues. Newspaper articles almost always lead with the seemingly obligatory marijuana pun, even articles about medical marijuana that are very sympathetic to the patients. This sends the message – to use a prohibitionist cliché -- that the issue is not to be taken seriously.
See
Ottawa Citizen Practices First Class Journalism
A Brilliantly Insightful Editorial: " Marijuana isn’t just a serious issue. It’s huge. "

Nonetheless, the fact remains that we are winning -- essentially for two reasons. The first is that the Drug War is rotting like the Soviet Union. The second is the anti-prohibitionists have an intrinsic advantage in using the Internet.
See
As People March Around the World, The Global Marijuana Resistance Movement Comes of Age – Thanks To The Internet.

The challenge to the cannabis communities is to get the media and sincerely concerned leaders that cannabis is an issue that must be taken seriously. This is something that no one else can do for us and that is really the ultimate purpose of MarijuanaNews.com.
